Now I'm verifying whether T01WORKSPACE can actually be reached through any pre-existing engineering-channel member who happens to also belong to that workspace, since the query chain doesn't strictly require matching the specific target user.

I realize the join structure only ties channels to messages by channel_id, not by user_id -- so the constraint that the same user who's a channel member also authored the matching message isn't actually enforced anywhere in the query logic.

This confirms a real defect: the prompt's phrasing implies the workspace member is the message author, but the compiled selector allows any workspace member of the channel to satisfy the binding regardless of who actually posted.

This is a real validity defect: the compiled query never enforces that the message author is the same person holding both memberships, only that some workspace member also belongs to a channel containing a matching message from anyone. The decoy structure happens to still produce the correct answer, but the semantic mismatch between design intent and actual query logic is genuine.

The compiled query would even match a non-member who authored a message in a channel with some unrelated member present, which breaks the requirement that the poster be the workspace member themselves. The route_nodes trace through WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP and MESSAGE conceptually implies the same user on both ends, but the compiled query severs that correspondence, confirming this as a validity defect.
